summary_paragraph: The patient, a homeless man with a history of systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, COPD, and hepatitis C, was admitted for worsening dyspnea and lower extremity edema. He was found to be in acute on chronic heart failure with significant fluid overload, confirmed by elevated proBNP and weight gain. He was treated with IV diuresis, which led to improvement in symptoms and a weight reduction from 104.8 kg to 99.2 kg. During the hospitalization, he experienced a syncopal episode with head strike, likely due to overdiuresis and hypotension; imaging ruled out acute intracranial or spinal injury. He also had persistent thrombocytopenia, newly diagnosed hepatitis B, and hemoptysis, which led to discontinuation of rivaroxaban. His right toe pain was not due to infection, and pain was managed with oxycodone. He was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for close outpatient follow-up in cardiology, pulmonology, hematology, and liver clinics.
